title: Taiwanese Association of Students at Tufts
content_html:
The Taiwanese Association of Students at Tufts (TAST) is a culture-oriented student organization at Tufts University founded in 1996. According to its JumboLife profile, TAST was established to spread the culture, language, and history of Taiwan through fun and creative events open to the Tufts community each semester. The organization is recognized and funded by the Tufts Community Union (TCU) Senate and participates in the Pan Asian Council (PAC), a collaborative body of Asian and Asian American interest and culture clubs on campus.

TAST offers a community for students who are Taiwanese or interested in Taiwanese culture. Throughout the year, the club plans and hosts events celebrating elements of Taiwanese culture and collaborates with other Taiwanese clubs at other universities. The organization maintains an active Instagram account (@tuftstast, 605 followers as of the time of research) and a Facebook page, and its legacy website remains accessible at ase.tufts.edu/tast. Its e-list on the Tufts mailing system was most recently updated for the 2024–25 school year, indicating continued active operation.

TAST has been a presence on campus for nearly three decades and has participated in the broader intercollegiate Taiwanese student network. In 1998, students at Tufts, Harvard, and MIT co-founded the Boston Intercollegiate Taiwanese Students Association (BITSA) to serve the many Taiwanese student communities in the Boston area, reflecting TAST’s early role in regional community building.
